translation: (Voiceover): The golden magic deer has come to Polavaram, oh; the golden magic deer has come to Polavaram, oh; it means to drown the forests and all living things, oh; it means to drown the forests and all living things, oh

Arrows and our lives, these two are all we have; arrows and our lives, these two are all we have; in death or in life, it is this forest.. in death or in life, it is this forest.. all you children of the forest, take up your bows and arrows; all you children of the forest, take up your bows and arrows; the golden magic deer has come to Polavaram, oh; it means to drown the forests and all living things, oh

Verse 1: Clearing podu plots, we worked this land into shape; clearing podu plots, we worked this land into shape; at the start of each year we spread manure on it; at the start of each year we spread manure on it; we guarded the crops from the wild boars; we guarded the crops from the wild boars; leaves and wild greens; we have lived eating leaves, we have survived on wild greens; we have lived eating leaves, we have survived on wild greens; we won't live away from the forest, we won't leave the land; we won't live away from the forest, we won't leave the land; the golden magic deer has come to Polavaram, oh; it means to drown the forests and all living things, oh; jummare jumma jummare jumma jumma jumma jummare jumma ho.. jummare jumma jummare jumma jumma jumma jummare jumma ho.. jummare jumma jummare jumma jumma jumma jummare jumma ho.. (refrain)

Verse 2: The Koya hamlets, like pictures among twigs and branches, oh; the Koya hamlets, like pictures among twigs and branches, oh; hens, goats and puppies are the Konda Reddis' companions, oh; hens, goats and puppies are the Konda Reddis' companions, oh; green vines hang all over the trellis, oh; green vines hang all over the trellis, oh; what's brewed in the pots, aha; with the tasty brew simmered in our pots; with the tasty brew simmered in our pots; we endured hunger, we rejoiced at festivals; we endured hunger, we rejoiced at festivals; the golden magic deer has come to Polavaram, oh; it means to drown the forests and all living things, oh

Verse 3: We became kin to the hills and valleys; we became kin to the hills and valleys; at dusk, leaving the day behind, we came home to the hamlet; at dusk, leaving the day behind, we came home to the hamlet; at night we danced and sang in the moonlight; at night we danced and sang in the moonlight; with the birds, with the fruits; how could we ever give up our friendship with the birds and the fruits? How could we ever give up our friendship with the birds and the fruits? In famine, it is this forest; in good seasons, it is this forest; in famine, it is this forest; in good seasons, it is this forest; the golden magic deer has come to Polavaram, oh; it means to drown the forests and all living things, oh

Verse 4: Handing it over to the companies, what land will you give us for our land? Handing it over to the companies, what land will you give us for our land? Cutting down the forests, what forest will you give for the forest? Cutting down the forests, what forest will you give for the forest? You have let termites eat away the Scheduled Area laws; you have let termites eat away the Scheduled Area laws; in our villages, our rule; in our villages, our rule, your rule does not hold here; in our villages, our rule, your rule does not hold here; you commit sins and then you offer compensation? You commit sins and then you offer compensation? The golden magic deer has come to Polavaram, oh; it means to drown the forests and all living things, oh

Verse 5: If you rip open our bellies, will golden eggs come out? If you rip open our bellies, will golden eggs come out? Wearing the hide of development, the multinationals will come; wearing the hide of development, the multinationals will come; in the name of water, you have lit fires here; in the name of water, you have lit fires here; the fields, the steamers; abandoning the fields, you laid royal roads for steamers; abandoning the fields, you laid royal roads for steamers; this is no Jalayagnam, what you bring is a watery grave; this is no Jalayagnam, what you bring is a watery grave; the golden magic deer has come to Polavaram, oh; it means to drown the forests and all living things, oh

Verse 6: The games of your golden magic deer won't work here; the games of your golden magic deer won't work here; the trade of the white-skinned thieves won't pass here; the trade of the white-skinned thieves won't pass here; the devil's proclainers will never reach our hamlet; the devil's proclainers will never reach our hamlet; spears and bows and arrows, bol! Spears and bows and arrows will stand up to your tyranny; spears and bows and arrows will stand up to your tyranny; they will protect us, the children of nature; they will protect us, the children of nature; they will protect us, the children of nature; they will protect us, the children of nature; they will protect us, the children of nature; they will protect us, the children of nature
summaryEn: Bangaru Mayaledi ('The Golden Magic Deer') is sung by Vimalakka on the album Vimalakka Hits (2023). It is a protest by forest-dwelling Adivasi communities against the Polavaram project, whose reservoir the song says will 'drown the forests and all living things'. The title image comes from the Ramayana. There a demon's golden-deer disguise lures Sita into danger; here it stands for a glittering promise of development that hides destruction. The opening verses speak in the voice of the Koya and Konda Reddi communities, describing a life bound to the forest: clearing podu plots, guarding crops from wild boar, living on leaves and wild greens, brewing drink in pots, dancing in the moonlight, and depending on the forest 'in famine and in good seasons'. With only 'arrows and our lives', they vow not to leave. The later verses turn sharply accusatory. They ask what land or forest can replace what is taken, and they charge that Scheduled Area laws have been left to the termites and that compensation cannot undo the sin. Development is called a hide worn by multinational companies. The irrigation drive is not 'Jalayagnam', the name of an irrigation programme, but a 'watery grave'. Rejecting 'white-skinned thieves' and the 'devil's proclainers' (earthmovers), it ends vowing that spears and bows will protect the children of nature.
summaryTe: ‘బంగారు మాయలేడి’ విమలక్క 2023 ‘విమలక్క హిట్స్’ ఆల్బమ్‌లో పాడిన పాట. ‘అడవులను, జీవులను ముంచేయ జూస్తున్న’ పోలవరం ప్రాజెక్టుపై అడవి బిడ్డలైన ఆదివాసీల నిరసన గీతం ఇది. రామాయణంలో సీతను ఆపదలోకి లాగిన మాయలేడి ఇక్కడ ‘అభివృద్ధి’ అనే మెరుపు వాగ్దానం వెనుక దాగిన వినాశనానికి ప్రతీక. మొదటి చరణాలు కోయ, కొండరెడ్ల గొంతుతో అడవితో ముడిపడిన బతుకును వర్ణిస్తాయి - పోడు కొట్టడం, అడవి పందుల నుంచి చేను కాపాడడం, ఆకులు, అలములు తిని బతకడం, కుండల్లో కాచిన సారా, వెన్నెల్లో ఆటపాటలు; ‘కరువైనా ఈ అడవే, కాలమైనా ఈ అడవే’. ‘బాణాలు, ప్రాణాలు - రెండే మాకున్నాయి’ అంటూ అడవిని, నేలను విడిచి పోమని ప్రతిజ్ఞ చేస్తారు. తర్వాతి చరణాల్లో పాట గొంతు పదునెక్కుతుంది: కంపెనీలకు కట్టబెట్టిన భూమికి బదులు ఏ భూమి ఇస్తావు? నరికిన అడవికి బదులు ఏ అడవి ఇస్తావు? షెడ్యూల్డ్ ప్రాంత చట్టాలకు చెదలు పట్టించారు; పాపాలు చేసి పరిహారం ఇస్తారా? అభివృద్ధి తోలు కప్పుకుని బహుళజాతి కంపెనీలు వస్తున్నాయి; ఇది ‘జలయజ్ఞం’ కాదు, జలసమాధి. ‘తెల్లతోలు దొంగలు’, ‘సైతాను ప్రొక్లెయిన్లు’ మా గూడేనికి రావని, బల్లాలు, విల్లంబులే ప్రకృతి బిడ్డలను కాపాడతాయని ధిక్కార ప్రతిజ్ఞతో పాట ముగుస్తుంది.
